content.content:
1. Necessity — the prerequisites fix one arrangement and no machine-checkable artifact of it: the store is opened on the repository's trunk state root; that root is reached from the invocation workspace's own repository entry (an entry that is the workspace's own resolves to that workspace's root, an entry that leads elsewhere resolves to the root it leads to, and an entry that cannot be followed refuses); the jj runner stays anchored on the invocation workspace, so the store root and the working copy the invocation edits are two answers to two questions; and an unreachable trunk refuses, naming the cause, with no fallback to the invocation workspace root. Which layouts resolve, to which root, which refuse, and how the runner anchor is kept, over every layout the rule admits, is unsettled until the model at `specs/state/root.qnt` fixes it. Fail if the model artifact could be dropped without loss.

2. Fidelity, both directions, applied to the model at `specs/state/root.qnt`, read against each prerequisite as each is recorded at check time:

a. No looser — every fact a prerequisite fixes is carried by the model, under the representation the model chooses:
   - the self case: an entry that is the invocation workspace's own yields that workspace's root as the store root;
   - the other case: an entry that leads to another working copy yields that working copy's root as the store root, and the model's check uses a target distinct from the invocation workspace so the two roots are shown distinct;
   - the unresolved case: an entry that cannot be followed to a working copy yields the refusal and never the invocation workspace's root;
   - the resolution starts from the invocation workspace and uses its own entry, with no other starting point and no fallback default;
   - the anchor: the jj runner's anchor is the invocation workspace root in every reachable state, and resolution does not replace it — after the store root is resolved to a root other than the invocation's, the runner anchor still equals the invocation workspace. The two roots coincide only in the self case, and that coincidence is an outcome of the place, not a rule tying the runner to the store.
   A fact the model omits, merges into another case, or leaves unconstrained is a loose divergence: name the fact and the prerequisite that fixes it. A model that resolves the store root but has no invocation-workspace root for the runner, or lets resolution assign that anchor, omits the anchor fact and is a loose divergence even if every resolution row is correct.

b. No stricter — the model requires, forbids or constrains nothing a prerequisite does not fix. The line around the unresolved entry is explicit:
   - The prerequisites fix three outcome shapes — the invocation workspace's own root, the led working copy's root, and the refusal — and delegate "the cases in which following the entry leaves the trunk unresolved" to the resolution. The model MAY therefore split the unresolved entry into any failure modes it chooses (missing, unreadable, dangling, or others) and may name the cause on the refusal; that split is not a strict divergence, provided every distinguished mode yields the refusal and no root.
   - The model MAY NOT add a fourth outcome shape, a resolvable case the text does not fix, a refusal for a layout the text leaves resolvable, a root for a layout the text leaves unresolvable, or a rule about an aspect the text leaves open — the entry's textual form, the shape or spelling of the path it leads to, how far such a root is followed, what may sit between the invocation and that root — and no fact about the modelling language's own representation carried as a rule about the trunk. A distinct refusal cause is not a strict divergence; a distinct resolution outcome or an extra resolvable case is.
   Read each such element against the recorded text at check time; any element, case or constraint the text does not fix is a strict divergence: name it and the rule it adds.

c. Clauses — where a prerequisite is recorded as requirement sentences, the model is read clause by clause against them: a clause whose observable the model does not distinguish, and an observable the model distinguishes that no clause states, are divergences, each named in the direction it falls. The clause list is that prerequisite's, read at check time; it is not restated here.

3. Executability and discrimination — the model must be a runnable Quint artifact whose checks discriminate, not a set of declarations that typechecks. With `quint` 0.33.1 (the house version), from the repository root:

   (i) `quint typecheck specs/state/root.qnt` — pass iff exit 0 with no diagnostics; fail otherwise.

   (ii) `quint test specs/state/root.qnt --main=<module>` — the model must define, under names it chooses, an executable `run` for each resolution case, each ending in an assertion of that case's outcome: the self case asserts the store root is the invocation workspace's root; the other case asserts the store root is the led working copy's root and that the led root differs from the invocation workspace; the unresolved case asserts the refusal and no root, and if the model splits that case, one run per distinguished failure mode. For the anchor, every run must assert the runner anchor equals the invocation workspace after resolution, and the other case must additionally assert the store root differs from the runner anchor. The runs must be discoverable by `quint test` (names ending in `Test`, or a `--match` the reviewer reads from the model). Pass iff `quint test` prints an `ok <name> passed` line for every case the model distinguishes and no failure; fail if a case or run is absent, a case's outcome or the anchor is not asserted, or a run fails. A model with abstract, undefined types and a stuttering `init`/`step` defines no runs: `quint test` prints only the module name and no `ok` lines, and the clause fails.

   (iii) The anchor must be machine-checked. If the model carries the runner anchor as a state component, it must define an invariant or temporal property (under a name it chooses) stating that the anchor equals the invocation workspace root in every reachable state, and `quint verify specs/state/root.qnt --main=<module> --invariant=<name> --max-steps=<N>` must report `NoError`; the reviewer identifies the invariant by reading the model and supplies its name. If the model instead carries the anchor as a frame condition on the resolution action, (ii)'s anchor assertions are the check, and the model must still define at least one invariant or temporal property for the resolution that `quint verify` checks. In either form, a model with no invocation-workspace root for the runner, or one that lets resolution assign it, fails (ii) and this clause.

   (iv) `quint run specs/state/root.qnt --main=<module> --max-steps=<N> --max-samples=<n> --out-itf=<tmp>.itf.json` — the checker must be shown to reach a non-initial state: the ITF trace must contain at least two distinct state valuations (a state other than state 0). Pass iff it does; fail iff every state equals the initial state (a stutter-only model). This is the direct check that the model is a transition system; it supplements, and does not replace, (ii) and (iii).

   The clause fixes no encoding: the carrier types, their constructors and equality remain the model's rule, and any carrier with decidable equality and constructible values satisfies (i)–(iv). It does not require a particular module name, type name or invariant name; `<module>`, `<name>` and the run names are read from the model.

The criterion names no element of the model's representation in advance: which fact, clause, extra rule or missing executable check is at issue is found while reading the artifact against the recorded prerequisites, and appears only in the finding. It tracks no wording of the dependent and survives a rewording of the dependent that leaves what it decides unchanged.
content.rationale:
The dependent is a formal model, and both of this unit's edges claim it: the prose decision that roots the store on the trunk, resolves it from the invocation workspace and keeps the jj runner on the invocation workspace is natural-to-code, and the requirement sentences restating it are structured-to-code. The check is therefore a review of the artifact against both prerequisites, with a fixed command suite; the form stays review-criteria with inline criteria because the model's every case is read against the recorded text, and the commands in clause 3 are run as part of the review and their output is the machine evidence.

This amendment replaces the previous clause 3 and tightens clauses 1–2. The old gate no longer covered the use for three reasons. First, its machine discriminator was false on quint 0.33.1: it said a declared type left without a definition is dropped by the flattener and every importing module then fails to flatten, but a model declaring all three types abstract with `init`/`step` that do nothing passes `quint typecheck` and `quint verify` (flatten plus three steps, `NoError`), and it imports fine. The clause therefore admitted exactly the stub it claimed to reject. The rewritten clause 3 requires a runnable artifact: the model's own `step`, a run per resolution case whose assertion `quint test` reports, an invariant or temporal property over the anchor that `quint verify` checks, and a `quint run` trace with a state other than the initial one. An abstract, stuttering stub defines no runs, no anchor invariant and no distinct state, so it cannot satisfy the clause; this is a real discriminator rather than a claim about flattening. Second, the necessity clause named the jj anchor but the fidelity criterion never required it, so a model could resolve the store root correctly and omit the second root. Clause 2a now requires the anchor as a fact (the runner anchor equals the invocation workspace in every reachable state, and resolution never assigns it), clause 3(ii) requires every row to assert it, and clause 3(iii) machine-checks it; a model missing the anchor, or letting it follow the resolved store root, fails. Third, clause 2b's "no repository-entry case beyond the ones the prerequisites name" was undecidable against a model that distinguishes Missing | Unreadable | Dangling, because the prerequisites delegate "the cases in which following the entry leaves the trunk unresolved" to the resolution. Clause 2b now states the line explicitly: splitting the unresolved entry into chosen failure modes and naming their causes is allowed; adding a fourth outcome shape, an extra resolvable case, or a rule about the entry's spelling, path shape or follow distance is not.

The criterion reads the prerequisites as recorded at check time, so it pins none of their wording and presupposes nothing their recorded text does not fix. It fixes no encoding: the carrier types and their names remain the model's rule. Red is the artifact's absence: with no `specs/state/root.qnt`, `quint typecheck` fails file-not-found and the criteria have nothing to read, so the resolution rule goes unenforced until the model exists in a runnable form. The commands in clause 3 are run as part of the review because a typecheck establishes only that the text parses, not that the checker can execute the resolution or that the runner anchor is kept.
